title: Europa International Gs
eyebrow: MERCEDES-BENZ G-CLASS · W463 · US VIA SANTA FE · 1993–2001
verdict: A small company in Santa Fe spent years and a lot of money proving to Washington that the G was legal, and ended up building the US market that Mercedes then bought from it. The trucks are simpler, plainer and often the better G to own.

paragraphs: Before 2002 you couldn't walk into a Mercedes dealer in America and buy a G-Class. You could buy one from Europa International in Santa Fe, New Mexico. Europa took the civilian [[g-class/w463|W463]], crash-tested and certified it at its own expense, and sold 300 GEs, G 320s and eventually V8 [[g-class/g500|G 500s]], federalized and certified for US sale. They were 50-state legal, not gray-market. In practice these are the first American G-Wagens.

story.heading: AMERICA SAYS NO
paragraphs: The G was never planned for the US. In the 1980s gray-market specialists brought [[g-class/w460|W460s]] in anyway, but tighter import rules in 1987 and the 1988 Imported Vehicle Safety Compliance Act largely ended that. Hagerty notes that gray-market buyers had always paid a steep premium, and Mike Serpe of Club G-Wagen warns that some of those dealers weren't entirely trustworthy. Anyone who wanted a G legally needed someone to do the certification properly.

According to the German Cars For Sale Blog, that was Dave Holland's idea. His Santa Fe company, Europa, decided to certify the truck to federal emissions and safety standards, crash tests included. Dealer Ferraris Online's account says the programme took five years, finished in October 1993 and cost $500,000. Wikipedia says Europa started selling Gs that year.

story.heading: FROM CONVERTER TO MANUFACTURER
paragraphs: The early trucks were European Gs modified to US specification. Hagerty says Europa later persuaded Mercedes to build them to DOT standards at the factory. Then came the bigger step. Ferraris Online says that after almost two years and more than $1 million, Europa gained US Small Volume Manufacturer status, making the trucks legal in all 50 states. Wikipedia ties that status to the arrival of the V8 G 500 in 1998 and says it made Europa the exclusive US importer and distributor.

The line-up followed Europe's. It started with the 3.0-litre inline-six 300 GE, then the 3.2-litre inline-six G 320. In 1998 the G 320 switched to a V6, so both engines exist for that year. The 5.0-litre V8 G 500 joined at the top, and Europa also certified a handful of short-wheelbase Cabriolets. Volumes were small and margins were large. Hagerty reports that some trucks sold for as much as $135,000.

story.heading: WHAT A EUROPA G IS LIKE
paragraphs: From outside, a 2000 Europa G 500 looks almost the same as a 2002 Mercedes-Benz USA truck. Jalopnik points to the black-painted bumpers, where later trucks have body-colour ones. Inside it's plainer: the steering wheel and instrument cluster come from the pre-facelift W210 E-Class, there are no radio buttons on the wheel, and the 722.6 five-speed automatic has no tip-shift gate. The dash-top screen on some trucks is Mercedes' optional navigation.

Under the skin it's still a full W463. Overland Journal's Scott Brady bought a 1996 Europa truck for the Expeditions West fleet. It had ABS, airbags and three dash buttons for the centre, rear and front locks, and Brady praised the early Europa Gs for their simple systems, durable six-cylinder engines and late-1990s build quality. German Cars For Sale Blog likes them for the same reason: fewer US-specific electronics to go wrong.

story.heading: THE HANDOVER
paragraphs: Europa's success was what ended its import business. Mercedes-Benz bought the US distribution rights and launched the G officially for the 2002 model year, with the G 500 and [[g-class/g55-amg|G 55 AMG]]. Europa moved into service, parts and accessories, and kept importing a few models America never got officially, such as the three-door Cabriolet. A related company, Europa G-Wagen LLC of Santa Fe, still appears in title histories as late as 2013. The importer itself is a footnote now, but its trucks are not: a Europa G is the sweet spot for anyone who wants a 1990s G with proper US paperwork.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE NEIMAN MARCUS G
callout.title: A G-Wagen in the Christmas catalogue
paragraphs: In 1999 Europa and Neiman Marcus put a special-edition G 500 in the department store's famous Christmas Book at $160,000. It had a two-tone interior and Swedish birch trim. According to German Cars For Sale Blog, six were sold, probably built to order, which makes it one of the rarest US-market Gs.
It also shows who Europa was selling to. These weren't farm trucks. The trucks were expensive and luxurious, and they were still capable off-road.

engineering_intro: Mechanically, Europa trucks are civilian W463s from the 1990s: a ladder frame, coil-sprung solid axles front and rear, permanent four-wheel drive with a two-speed transfer case, and three differential locks on the dash. The differences are in the engines and the amount of electronics. The sixes and the M113 V8 run without the COMAND and smart-key systems that came with Mercedes-Benz USA's 2002 trucks.

engineering.note: Separate steel frame; LWB five-door, plus a few SWB Cabriolets.
Coil-sprung and link-located, as on every W463 until 2018.
Two-speed transfer case with low range.
Three dash buttons, confirmed on a 1996 Europa truck.
Four-speed automatic on the I6 G 320; 722.6 five-speed on the G 500.

engineering_note.title: HOW TO SPOT ONE
engineering_note.body: A pre-2002 G with a US-format VIN and a federal compliance label is the basic sign. On a G 500, look for the W210 E-Class steering wheel and cluster, no radio buttons on the wheel, and black-painted bumpers. Ask for any Europa sales or service paperwork too.

generations_table.note: Europa started selling in 1993 after finishing certification
Four-speed automatic; head-gasket seep is the known weakness
1998 was the changeover year, so both engines exist
722.6 five-speed; arrived with Europa's Small Volume Manufacturer status
Fewer than ten certified as US models, per Ferraris Online

buying_checks.head: US VIN and Europa paperwork
buying_checks.body: A real Europa truck has a US VIN and federal compliance, not a foreign VIN cleared later by an independent lab. Match the VIN, the compliance label and any Europa invoices.

buying_checks.head: Which G 320 engine?
buying_checks.body: 1998 was the changeover year, so a G 320 can have the M104 inline-six or the M112 V6. Check the engine code, since the two have different weak points.

buying_checks.head: M104 head gasket
buying_checks.body: Look under the right rear of the inline-six for oil seeping from the head gasket. Owners say a proper repair, about $2,000 at a dealer in 2002, usually lasts.

buying_checks.head: Front axle service history
buying_checks.body: Ask when the front knuckles and bearings were last repacked. Europa recommended every 40,000 miles; owners say it's definitely due by 75,000.

buying_checks.head: Test all three lockers
buying_checks.body: Engage centre, rear and front on loose ground and watch the indicators. Lockers that 'were never used' often don't work.

buying_checks.head: Ignition and key system
buying_checks.body: German Cars For Sale Blog warns that the EIS and smart-key system on later trucks can strand you without warning, and one Europa G 320 needed a new ignition tumbler. Make sure every key starts the truck.

buying_checks.head: Rust from snowy states
buying_checks.body: Scott Brady's 1996 Europa truck had two corrosion spots from its time in the Northeast. Check the tailgate's lower edge, door bottoms, sills and rear frame tubes.

buying_checks.head: Originality pays
buying_checks.body: Hagerty says enthusiasts will pay up to 30 per cent more for an all-original G. Keep the factory parts if you modify one.

repairs.title: Front axle repack (knuckles & wheel bearings)
repairs.symptoms: Grease weeping from the swivels, torn CV boots, wheel-bearing noise or play, or no record of the job.
repairs.fix: Strip the front hubs and knuckles, replace the CV boots and wheel bearings, and repack. Europa's own interval was 40,000 miles. Bearing clearances are critical, and one owner found local Mercedes dealers didn't know the job, so use a G-experienced technician if you lack the factory procedure and a dial indicator.
repairs.tools: Factory procedure · hub nut socket · dial indicator · CV boots · wheel bearings · grease · seals

parts.name: Genuine Mercedes front wheel bearing, outer 009 981 48 05 — listed for 2002+ W463; confirm fit by VIN
Genuine Mercedes front wheel seal 463 334 01 59 — listed for 2002+ W463; confirm fit by VIN

repairs.title: M104 head-gasket seep (I6 G 320)
repairs.symptoms: Oil seeping at the right rear of the cylinder head, visible from underneath; oil smell after a run.
repairs.fix: Replace the head gasket and resurface the head if needed, with new head bolts and seals. Owners report the leak doesn't return after a proper repair. A later Europa seller still recommended the G 300 or G 500 over the inline-six G 320 for this reason.
repairs.tools: Head gasket set · head bolts · torque wrench and angle gauge · access to a machine shop

parts.name: Elring M104 3.2 head gasket 104 016 28 20 (E320/S320 3.2 — confirm vs G 320 engine no.)
Elring M104 head gasket set 104 010 37 20 (confirm vs engine no.)
Elring M104 head bolt set 104 990 00 12

repairs.title: Harmonic balancer (V6 & V8)
repairs.symptoms: On the M112 V6 and M113 V8, vibration at idle, a wobbling crank pulley, cracked or bulging rubber, or belt chirp that changes with revs. If the outer ring separates you lose the belt drive.
repairs.fix: Remove the belt, lock the crank, and replace the balancer with a new centre bolt and front crank seal. Use a new balancer, not a used one.
repairs.tools: Crank counter-hold tool · 27 mm socket · breaker bar or high-torque impact · balancer · centre bolt · crank seal

parts.name: Corteco harmonic balancer / crank pulley 112 035 14 00 (M112/M113)
Corteco front crankshaft seal 023 997 84 47
CTA crank pulley counterhold tool 7270

repairs.title: Front axle seal leak
repairs.symptoms: Gear oil on the inner front wheels or calipers, brakes pulling to one side.
repairs.fix: Replace both front axle seals and check the shafts. Replace the pads and resurface the rotors if oil has reached them. It makes sense to do this with the axle repack.
repairs.tools: Axle seals · seal driver · gear oil · pads/rotors if contaminated

parts.name: Genuine Mercedes front axle shaft seal 009 997 28 47 — listed for 2002+ W463; confirm fit by VIN
Red Line 75W-90 GL-5 gear oil (1 qt)

repairs.title: Diff locks won't engage
repairs.symptoms: One or all locks won't engage, or drop out. It's usually the vacuum system, not the differentials.
repairs.fix: Confirm vacuum at the actuators, then trace back through the reservoir, hoses and switchover valves with a tee-in gauge. Split connectors and perished rubber fittings are common. Change the diff and transfer-case fluids while you're in there.
repairs.tools: Hand vacuum pump with gauge · vacuum tees and line · connectors · gear oil

parts.name: Lisle 20300 vacuum gauge / pump tester
Genuine Mercedes vacuum hose 000 158 14 35
Red Line 75W-90 GL-5 gear oil (1 qt)

repairs.title: Steering damper & front-end wander
repairs.symptoms: Wander and shake at 55–70 mph, vague on-centre feel, front-end clunks.
repairs.fix: Replace the steering damper, check the drag link and tie-rod ends, then align. Some Europa trucks, like Jalopnik's 2000 G 500, already have an aftermarket stabiliser; check that it isn't worn out.
repairs.tools: Steering damper · sockets and wrenches · tie-rod/drag-link ends if worn

parts.name: Stabilus steering damper 463 463 00 32 — listed for 2002+ W463; confirm fit by VIN
Febi drag link / tie-rod end — listed for 2002+ W463; confirm fit by VIN

repairs.title: Rust on the frame and body
repairs.symptoms: Bubbling at the tailgate's lower edge, door bottoms and sills; scale on the rear frame tubes and strut mounts.
repairs.fix: Blast and treat early, or weld in repair panels. Cavity-wax the doors and underbody and rinse off salt after winter. On a 25-year-old truck from a snowy state, inspect before you buy, not after.
repairs.tools: Wire wheel or blaster · rust converter and primer · cavity wax · welder

parts.name: Eastwood Internal Frame Coating (cavity wax for frame rails)
Eastwood Rust Encapsulator + Internal Frame Coating Plus kit

faq.q: Is a Europa G a gray-market truck?
faq.a: No. Europa certified the trucks to US emissions and safety standards, including crash testing, sold them with US VINs, and gained Small Volume Manufacturer status, making them 50-state legal. Gray-market Gs were private imports cleared one at a time.

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: About 33 inches. An Expedition Portal owner runs 275/70R18 on an unlifted 2000 G 500 and only rubbed on aftermarket ET63 wheels. Another runs 285/65R18 with a slight rub at full left lock. Another owner says up to about 32 inches should clear with no rubbing. Have the tire size re-coded with Mercedes diagnostics so the speedometer and ESP stay accurate.

faq.q: Which Europa G should I buy?
faq.a: Forum regulars usually prefer the G 500 for its much greater power at similar mileage. German Cars For Sale Blog prefers the 300 GE or G 500 to the inline-six G 320 because of its head-gasket issue. One owner found the V6 G 320 more economical than a G 500, though the gap narrows when towing.

faq.q: Do Europa trucks have all three lockers?
faq.a: Yes. Scott Brady's 1996 Europa truck had dash buttons for the centre, rear and front locks, plus ABS and airbags.

faq.q: How is a Europa G 500 different from a 2002 Mercedes-Benz USA G 500?
faq.a: It looks nearly the same outside, apart from black-painted bumpers. Inside it has a pre-facelift W210 E-Class steering wheel and cluster, no wheel-mounted radio controls, older climate control, and a 722.6 automatic without the tip-shift gate. It also avoids the COMAND electronics that German Cars For Sale Blog blames for early MBUSA trucks' electrical problems.

faq.q: How much did they cost new?
faq.a: Hagerty says some sold for up to $135,000. The 1999 Neiman Marcus Christmas-catalogue G 500 was $160,000, and six were sold.

Usually about the same as 2002-on trucks. Recent asks include a 202,750-mile 2000 G 500 at $32,000 (Jalopnik) and a well-documented 1998 G 320 at $47,500 (German Cars For Sale Blog), which the blog called high but understandable. Clean Europa G 320s come up only every few years and tend to sell quickly.
We couldn't find a reliable total. The rarest variant is better documented: fewer than ten short-wheelbase Cabriolets were certified as US models, according to Ferraris Online.

faq.q: How often should the front axle be serviced?
faq.a: Europa recommended repacking the front axle (knuckles, wheel bearings, CV boots) every 40,000 miles. One owner thought that was early but agreed it's needed by about 75,000. Expect to pay around $1,500–2,000 at a specialist (2002 figures).

Yes, by most accounts. Scott Brady put a 1996 Europa G into the Expeditions West fleet, and its previous owner had driven it from the Northeast to Labrador and Newfoundland with a fridge, compressor and winch. Brady expected it to last another 10–15 years without major problems.

mods.why: Complete G-specific builds with lift, armour, racks, lighting and storage, done as one coherent truck.
Sympathetic restorations for owners who want factory-correct, which is where the value premium is.
Lift springs and better shocks to clear 33s and carry overland weight.
Flat platform racks for tents, recovery gear and spares.
A brush guard and tucked running boards are common first additions. The 2000 G 500 in an Expedition Portal sale wore an ARB guard, and Jalopnik's 2000 G 500 had a skid plate and tucked steps.
A 33-inch all-terrain on 18-inch wheels at a sensible offset makes the biggest difference for the least money.

baseline_service.intro: Start by confirming exactly what you bought: a Europa truck can have the M103, M104 or M112 six or the M113 V8, a 4- or 5-speed automatic, and drivetrain fluids that changed through the 1990s. Then reset everything — these are 25-plus-year-old grey-market imports, and service records rarely made the trip.
